correctness.rationale: For the fixed convex body |X_i|<=2 and sum|X_i|<=3, its 24 vertices are signed permutations of (0,1,2). A generic central plane intersects one segment per crossed facet. Sorting normal absolute coordinates x>y>z>0 gives six square-facet crossings 2[x>2y]+2[x>2z] and eight hexagonal-facet crossings 4+2[y<2z]; thus N=4+2([x>2y]+[x>2z]+[y<2z]) takes only 6,8,10. In a signed-permutation chamber (area pi/12), the ten-gon domain is triangle VTC and the eight-gon domains UVT and TWC; their normalized solid angles yield the exact arctangent law p6=0.4984506899, p8=0.3161088556, p10=0.1854404545. The full-sphere result follows from the 48 symmetric chambers, not numerical sampling. Independently compared crossed facets, crossed edges and indicator count for 3647 generic integer normals; agreement, with analytic facet proof establishing continuum.
